question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 1.
solution:
The correct answer is '**has been**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The passage refers to an ongoing issue starting from the 19th century and continuing into the present time, making "has been" the most appropriate choice.
 
• "Has been" is the present perfect tense, which is used to describe actions that started in the past and continue to the present.
 
• Other options ("have been", "was been", "had been") do not fit grammatically or contextually for the ongoing nature of the problem described in the passage.

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 4**'.

 

Complete Passage: *Erosion of America's farmland by wind and water (1) has been__ a problem since settlers first put the prairies and grasslands (2)______ the plow in the 19th century. By the 1930s, more than 282 million acres of farmland were (3)______ by erosion. After 40 years of conservation efforts, soil erosion has (4)________ due to new demands placed (5)____ the land by heavy crop production.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• "Has been" indicates an ongoing problem that started in the past and continues into the present, which is the correct meaning for the context of the passage.
 
• "Have been" would be incorrect because the subject "erosion" is singular, requiring the singular verb form "has been".
 
• "Was been" and "had been" do not fit in the context, as they suggest completed actions in the past, which does not align with the passage's context about an ongoing issue.
